newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian customs report increase port revenues.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian customs report increase port revenues.

text.p: Earnings from Nigeria's ports shot up to 69.3 billion naira by November 1996 from 47.4 billion naira in all 1995, the customs agency's chief executive said.

Brigadier-General Samuel Ango said 48.4 billion naira of the income represented import and excise duties while 20.5 billion naira was collected on behalf of government agencies, the independent Guardian newspaper reported on Monday.

Ango said seven percent of the 20.5 billion naira was collected as surchages on port facilities for the Nigerian Ports Authorities while five percent was for imported sugar for the National Sugar Development Council.
Two percent of the money was collected on imported vehicles for the National Automotive Council and five percent was for the Federal Inland Revenue Services from value added tax on goods.
The collection of customs dues at Nigerian ports was tightened last year after the Federal Finance Ministry said there was laxity and corruption in the customs service.
